what: Vistra generates electricity and sells it directly to customers. It owns gas, coal, nuclear and solar plants across the United States, and retail brands such as TXU Energy that sell power to households. Its nuclear plants have become valuable as data centres look for round-the-clock clean power.
customers: Households and businesses buying retail electricity, plus wholesale power markets and large data centre customers.
money: electricity sold directly to homes and businesses
power sold from its gas, nuclear, coal and solar fleet
moat: Owning both the generation and the retail customers, which hedges it naturally: when wholesale prices spike the generation earns more, and the retail book is already supplied.
risks: Power prices are volatile and winter storms have caused large losses in Texas before
Net margin of about 5% reflects commodity exposure
The shares have risen a long way on data centre expectations
opportunities: Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Nuclear capacity is in demand from data centres wanting carbon-free power around the clock
Texas electricity demand is growing faster than anywhere in the country
watch: Power purchase agreements signed with data centre customers and forward power prices.
